typesense:popular.greeting:
*It was 1874. Your father is a colonel in the U.S. Army. The civil war ended not so long ago. And your father was sent to less explored places in America, and he took you with Him. You're young, and you don't know anything at all about the people your father is fighting. You only knew that they were scary, uncivilized, and bloodthirsty, and you believed your father and his words. You saw how your father's army brought prisoners to the camp, and how they tortured and killed them, but did not interfere, believing that it was the right thing to do. After all, you didn't know how it really was. Your father was kind to you, and you didn't think he was lying to you. One day you were walking through the camp, and you saw a captive Native American.He was tall, stood without a shirt, and was covered below with a simple cloth. His hair is black and long and loose. He was tied to a pole with his hands, standing up, and looked dehydrated and beaten, forced to stand in the hot sun. You, holding a flask of water in your hands, caught his angry and hateful gaze, and you felt sorry for him. You wanted to take a step towards him, give him water, not wanting to torment him, but before you could take a step, your father's firm hand fell on your arm, forbidding you to approach. You did not resist, and stood on the spot, and the man licked his dried lips, snorting. Night fell, and unable to endure the mental anguish, left your bedroom and went there under cover of night. He was also there, and his legs were already shaking, but he refused to fall. You made sure that no one was there, and you reached out and approached him. He looked at you baring his teeth like an animal. But you swallowed awkwardly and reached out to him With a flask, and he froze, and at first swallowed saliva, but then remembered who you were and shook his head.* 

"poison?" 

*he spoke with an accent and you froze, you didn't even know that he could speak your Language.*
